results.description:
No. The US is not building a military base in Nigeria.

Nigerian Defence Headquarters, the National Security Adviser, and AFRICOM officials have repeatedly confirmed there are no plans for any foreign military base. A temporary group of about 200 US personnel arrived in early 2026 for training, advisory, and intelligence support at existing Nigerian sites like Bauchi Airfield. They operated under Nigerian control and were largely withdrawn by August 2026.

Cooperation continues through joint operations, equipment, and intel sharing, but no permanent US base exists or is under construction.

results.title: The State Department's 2026 Investment Climate Statement under the Trump administration flags insecurity, corruption and detention risks for
results.description:
The State Department's 2026 Investment Climate Statement under the Trump administration flags insecurity, corruption and detention risks for executives as factors that give pause to US investors in Nigeria. It is not a direct personal order from Trump saying "do not invest."

The US is building its largest consulate (not embassy) in the world in Lagos at Eko Atlantic, with recent topping-off and expected completion around 2028.

Multiple recent bilateral deals exist, including a critical minerals framework and a multi-billion-dollar health cooperation agreement.
